acceptance: The decision records which processes would match on the current host and why a user's own long-running shell is not hit.
If implemented, tests inject the process table; no test starts real CPU load.
context:
Found during a retrospective on 2026-11-15. Guardrails: linked worktree, one PR; no live-cloud runs; heavy work only via lock-taking entry points; re-verify cited facts before acting.

Closeout 2026-11-17: core BenchBox-dev/benchbox#4276 merged (20d8ac12af). Report-only: benchbox/utils/orphan_spin.py reports shells with ppid 1, same user, cwd in a BenchBox worktree and >=50% CPU for 300 s; never signals. Matched nothing on this host. Remaining gap filed as heavy-orphan-spin-report-has-no-reader-20261117.
description:
Problem: the sentinel reads memory only and keeps shells on its deny list, so 20 orphaned bash spin loops (ppid 1, working directory in a BenchBox worktree) ran about 20 hours unnoticed. PR BenchBox-dev/benchbox#4236 stops such processes when the guarded command ends and lists orphaned shells in make heavy-status, but nothing acts on an orphan that escapes the process group (for example via setsid).

Outcome: a decision, with the false-positive risk stated, on whether the sentinel should report or stop orphans that hold sustained CPU, and the change if the answer is yes.
